# appsignal_log_view (Resource)



## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "appsignal_app" "example" {
  name        = "my-example-app"
  environment = "production"
}

resource "appsignal_log_source" "example" {
  app_id = appsignal_app.example.id

  name = "my-example-log-source"
  fmt  = "AUTODETECT"
  type = "application"
}

resource "appsignal_log_view" "example" {
  app_id = appsignal_app.example.id

  source_ids = [appsignal_log_source.example.id]

  name = "my-view"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `app_id` (String) The ID of the app to which the log view belongs.
- `name` (String) The name of the log view.

### Optional

- `columns` (Set of String) The columns to include in the log view.
- `line_height` (String) The line height of the log view. Defaults to `0`, the value AppSignal itself assigns.
- `query` (String) The query string that is used for the log view. Defaults to an empty string.
- `severities` (Set of String) The severities the log view matches. Each one of: `TRACE`, `DEBUG`, `INFO`, `NOTICE`, `WARN`, `ERROR`, `CRITICAL`, `ALERT`, `FATAL`, `UNKNOWN`.
- `source_ids` (Set of String) The IDs of the log sources which this view aggregates.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the log view.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import appsignal_log_view.example "<app_id>,<log_view_id>"
```
